chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about camels and cattle, which of them is better to be sacrificed with? He said: 'Those with full teeth (thawat al-arham).' And I asked him about their ages, so he said: 'As for cattle, it does not matter to you with which of their ages you sacrifice; and as for camels, only the two-year-old (thani) and above are suitable.'

key_terms.ذَوَاتُ اَلْأَرْحَامِ: Those with full teeth (a technical term indicating maturity, literally 'those of the wombs/bellies')
key_terms.يُضَحَّى: To be sacrificed (as a ritual offering)

ai.seo_question: What are the age and condition requirements for camels and cattle used in Islamic sacrifice?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the criteria for *udhiyah*, defining 'those with full teeth' (ذوات الأرحام) as the preferred standard for validity. While cattle sacrifice allows for flexibility regarding age, the hadith strictly mandates that camels must be at least two years old (thani), reflecting the distinct biological and legal classifications in Shia fiqh. This distinction highlights the precision required in ritual purity and the adherence to prophetic traditions in selecting sacrificial animals.
